what: Store::map refuses a record put by this process and not yet committed (StoreError::Uncommitted), while Store::read serves it from the writer. A surface is a plain (mapped) record, and a dependent unit's tasks read the surface its dependency filed earlier in the same request, so the host keeps its own copy of every surface it put and answers from it.
cost: a second copy of every surface written in a request, a sorted side table in the host, and a branch on every surface read
cause: the store's contract says a put is readable at once, but mapping needs a segment and the writer's buffer is not one; the trait gives no way to borrow uncommitted bytes for the request's life
class: a read interface whose answer depends on whether the bytes are committed, so every caller grows its own cache of what it wrote
